overview: Eswatini, formerly called Swaziland, is a small landlocked country in southern Africa, almost surrounded by South Africa. Its administrative capital is Mbabane, and Lobamba is its royal and legislative capital. Eswatini became independent from the United Kingdom in 1968 and is one of the last absolute monarchies in the world.

geography.text: For its size, Eswatini has very varied landscapes. It steps down from the cool, mountainous highveld in the west, through the hilly middleveld, to the hot, dry lowveld in the east, with the Lebombo Mountains along the border with Mozambique.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mild in the highlands, warmer in the lowveld.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Rhinos, elephants and lions in its reserves.

history.text: The Swazi kingdom was formed in the 1700s and 1800s under kings such as Sobhuza I and Mswati II, who gave the people their name. Britain made it a protectorate after the Boer War. Eswatini became independent in 1968 and is one of the world's last absolute monarchies. It was known as Swaziland until 2018.

events.title: Mswati II
events.text: Mswati II becomes king and expands the kingdom.

events.title: British rule
events.text: Britain takes over after the Boer War.

events.title: Absolute monarchy
events.text: King Sobhuza II suspends the constitution.

government.text: Eswatini is Africa's last absolute monarchy. King Mswati III, who has reigned since 1986, appoints the Prime Minister and much of parliament. Political parties cannot take part in elections. Protests in 2021 were violently suppressed.

economy.text: Eswatini's economy is closely tied to South Africa. Sugar, soft drink concentrate and textiles are its main exports.

culture.text: Swazi traditions remain strong. The Umhlanga, or Reed Dance, brings tens of thousands of young women to the royal residence each year. Incwala is a sacred kingship ceremony.

items.text: The Reed Dance, a yearly festival.

items.title: Mlilwane
items.text: A wildlife sanctuary in the Ezulwini Valley.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Sishwala, a thick porridge, with meat stews.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Candle making and glass blowing are popular crafts.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: The Umhlanga Reed Dance and the Incwala kingship ceremony.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and the national team is nicknamed Sihlangu Semnikati, after a royal shield. Wildlife reserves and mountain trails also make Eswatini popular for hiking and cycling.

didYouKnow: Eswatini is one of the last absolute monarchies in the world.
The country changed its name from Swaziland in 2018.
